title: TikTok: House vs ETF – who wins after 30 years (animated)
_sources: Zillow Sept 2026 market report: typical home value $366,913, typical rent (ZORI) $1,932, rent +2.7% y/y (model: +3%/yr). Freddie Mac PMMS 2026-10-22: 30y fixed 7.32%. ATTOM 2025: effective property tax ~0.9%. Maintenance 1%/yr (rule of thumb). Case-Shiller national (FRED CSUSHPINSA) 63.73 Jan 1987 -> 337.31 Jul 2026 = 4.31%/yr. S&P 500 incl. dividends ~10%/yr 1928-2025 (NYU Stern/Damodaran). Own model: 20% down $73,383, payment $2,016 + tax $275 + repairs $306 = $2,597/mo; renter invests $73,383 + difference. Year 30 net worth: buyer $1,356,851 (house $1.30M + $56k invested), renter $2,110,741; renter ahead from year 12. At 8%: buyer $1,352,370 vs renter $1,261,874. Excludes closing/selling costs, insurance, taxes on gains.

lines.text: Should you buy a house, or invest in an ETF? In thirty years, one of them makes you seven hundred fifty thousand dollars more.
Both start with the same seventy-three thousand dollars.
The buyer gets a three sixty-seven thousand dollar home at seven point three percent.
Loan, taxes and repairs: about twenty-six hundred a month.
The renter pays nineteen thirty-two, and invests the rest in an ETF.
For eleven years, the house is ahead. Then compound interest takes over.
After thirty years: house, one point three six million. ETF, two point one million.
But only at ten percent a year. At eight, the house wins. Which would you pick:
